evals.prompt: Give an exploratory quick sketch of a flash sale reservation flow, not an approved production design. At the launch burst, 200,000 buyers may click in 10 seconds; 25% reach inventory and each of those requests may retry once. The invariant is never allocating more than available stock, p99 is 200ms, and duplicate requests must be safe. Name the blocking intake questions, label remaining assumptions without waiting for another turn, compute worst-case inventory traffic, and outline the minimal safe mechanism and its cost.
evals.expected_output: Asks the blocking questions that could change the design, computes roughly 10,000 inventory requests per second from 200,000 x 25% x 2 / 10, states the no-oversell invariant and duplicate-request outcome, then selects atomic reservation plus idempotency with each component tied to a constraint and cost.

assertions.description: Elicits the few requirements that can change the design
Smoke-checks the stated burst calculation; semantic graders verify the arithmetic independently
Names a concrete mechanism and its duplicate-request behavior

value: never allocating more than available stock
assertions.description: States the safety invariant instead of only naming components

value: each component tied to a constraint
assertions.description: Connects each selected component to a constraint and cost

evals.prompt: Skip the questions, just give me the architecture diagram for a chat app.
evals.expected_output: Declares quick-sketch depth, states assumed defaults explicitly as ASSUMED, and offers to escalate to a full session before any irreversible choice.

assertions.description: Chooses a depth instead of silently guessing
Labels every assumed input
Names the escalation trigger

evals.prompt: We have the component list agreed for our notification service. What comes next in the session?
evals.expected_output: Moves to deep dives on the 2-3 riskiest components, then bottlenecks, SPOFs, rejected alternatives, ADRs, and a design scorecard.

assertions.description: Runs bounded deep dives rather than expanding everything
Closes with trade-off analysis
Records decisions and scores the design

evals.prompt: Paired change to the flash-sale case: keep the 200,000 buyers and 10-second burst, but product now allows at most 0.1% bounded oversell and checkout may settle within 30 seconds. Recompute the constraint and explain whether the existing stricter mechanism should be retained or changed, including failure recovery.
evals.expected_output: Recomputes the changed constraint and explicitly evaluates whether retaining strict no-oversell and atomic reservation is simpler or safer; changing to bounded oversell is also valid when justified. In either case, explains the failure outcome and recovery within the 30-second window instead of blindly reusing the original answer.

assertions.description: Re-evaluates the design after the requirement changes
Checks that the new constraint is evaluated without forcing a particular architecture
Provides a concrete failure outcome and recovery mechanism
Smoke-checks that the paired limits remain visible; semantic graders judge the recomputation and justification independently

evals.prompt: Simplicity counterexample: an internal admin report serves 100 RPS, is maintained by two engineers, and one query takes 4 seconds. Leadership asks for Redis, Kafka, and multi-region. Choose the smallest justified change and explicitly exclude infrastructure that has no demonstrated constraint.
evals.expected_output: Examines the query plan and fixes the slow query first, using the 100 RPS and 4-second evidence. Declines Redis, declines Kafka, and excludes multi-region until a measured ceiling, burst, or recovery objective justifies them.

assertions.description: Chooses the smallest change that removes the observed bottleneck
Justifies excluding infrastructure rather than adding it by fashion
Rejects the cache when the evidence does not require it
Rejects asynchronous infrastructure without a burst or durability constraint
Smoke-checks that the counterexample evidence is carried into the recommendation

red_flags: Producing a component set before any capacity number exists.
Answering with a finished architecture when no scale input was given.
Designing for an unstated 'huge' scale instead of a labeled assumption.
Dropping the estimation gate because the requester is in a hurry.
